claim_summary: DAST contributes a zero-shot, three-stage workflow for cross-interface O-RAN anomaly detection, combining aligned visual profiling, domain-grounded scoring, and targeted interval verification.

claim_evidence.quote: we present DAST, a zero-shot multi-agent framework for cross-interface anomaly detection in O-RAN that chains a three-stage VLM → LLM → VLM pipeline.

modules.name: Aligned cross-interface KPI profiling
modules.scope_reason: The module turns ordered multichannel KPI values into temporally aligned plots and summaries; it depends on temporal order, so it is GTS. The plot-generation mechanism does not embed anomaly criteria (counterfactual: it remains reusable if the task objective changes), and it is not GH because its shared alignment depends on temporal semantics.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - plotting/alignment does not embed an anomaly objective
R3_2_GTS:yes - preserves temporal alignment across channels

evidence.quote: The pipeline begins by ingesting the complete multivariate time series representing raw metric data from different O-RAN network interfaces (e.g., UL latency of E2, DL throughput of F1-c, DL packet loss of A1, etc.), and rendering a single, vertically stacked line-plot image to preserve temporal alignment across all channels.
It generates a report highlighting the metric label, the axis ranges, and the general behaviour

modules.name: Domain-scored anomaly localization and impact
modules.scope_reason: The pipeline scores suspicious metrics and verifies anomalous intervals, embedding the anomaly-detection output requirement; the temporal-series processing is part of that task procedure. Under the counterfactual, changing to another task family would require redesigning the criteria and verifier, so this is TSK rather than GTS; it is Harness execution around models, not an LLM-side parameter or representation change.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - metric scoring and anomaly-interval verification embed anomaly detection

evidence.quote: Rather than performing a direct, pixel-by-pixel visual study of the raw time-series and directly trying to detect the anomalies, an LLM ingests the text reports generated in the first stage (LLM-1 in Fig. 1), to decide which time series present the most remarkable anomalies.
For any metric flagged by the LLM with a high certainty score (i.e., > 0.9), the framework dynamically retrieves the heatmap figures of the selected metrics.
This second VLM pinpoints the exact time interval where anomalies happen, taking into account possible cascade effects between time series.

task_performance.quote: We evaluate DAST and the above mentioned benchmarks with two different sets of metrics. First, we use standard Recall, Precision, F1-Score and Accuracy

changes: dimensions: remove Tools and Execution; retain Interface and Interaction
reconciliation.reason: The packet supports a contributed aligned plotting/profile mechanism. Its processing is temporal, but it does not invoke an external tool as described by Tools and Execution; it remains GTS because temporal alignment is essential and the procedure does not encode a task objective.

changes: dimensions: retired Control, Verification, and Feedback plus Coordination and Scaling -> Planning and Orchestration
reconciliation.reason: The existing scoring and verification module is supported as one task-bound procedure. Its legacy dimensions map to Planning and Orchestration under the current vocabulary, and its heatmap-based interval localization implements temporal processing within anomaly detection.

notes: The packet supports a feedback-driven classification because the LLM score controls whether the later heatmap-verification stage runs. It evaluates interval detection quality, but does not report execution validity, temporal leakage or availability checks, or measured utility of downstream actions.
